hints: Remember the Brønsted-Lowry definition simply means a proton, $H^+$, donor is the acid and a proton acceptor is the base.
Look at reaction 2 first, $\text{HSO}_4^- + \text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{SO}_4^{2-} + \text{NH}_4^+$, and ask yourself whether $\text{NH}_3$ gains or loses $H^+$.
Now check reaction 1 for a $\text{NH}_3$ that loses $H^+$ to form $\text{NH}_2^-$, and check reaction 3 for any $H^+$ transfer at all.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Brønsted-Lowry test**

Think acid means donates $H^+$, base means accepts $H^+$. So just follow the hydrogen atoms.

Rule to apply:
$$\text{acid} \rightarrow \text{conjugate base} + H^+$$

**Analyse reaction 1**

One $\text{NH}_3$ becomes $\text{NH}_4^+$, it has gained $H^+$, so it is a base. The other $\text{NH}_3$ becomes $\text{NH}_2^-$, it has lost $H^+$, so it is an acid.

$$2\text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{NH}_2^- + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Analyse reaction 2**

Here $\text{HSO}_4^-$ loses $H^+$ to become $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, so it is the acid. $\text{NH}_3$ gains $H^+$ to become $\text{NH}_4^+$, so it is the base, not the acid.

$$\text{HSO}_4^- + \text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{SO}_4^{2-} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Analyse reaction 3 and conclude**

No $H^+$ is transferred at all. $\text{NH}_3$ uses its lone pair to bond to $\text{Ag}^+$, so it is acting as a Lewis base, not a Brønsted-Lowry acid.

$$\text{Ag}^+ + 2\text{NH}_3 \rightarrow [\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$$
Only reaction 1 shows $\text{NH}_3$ acting as a Brønsted-Lowry acid.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean $\text{NH}_3$ donates $H^+$ in all three reactions. Reaction 2 shows $\text{NH}_3$ accepting $H^+$, and reaction 3 shows no $H^+$ transfer at all.
options.B: Incorrect. While reaction 1 is correct, reaction 2 is not. Students often spot $\text{NH}_4^+$ as a product and assume $\text{NH}_3$ was the acid, but forming $\text{NH}_4^+$ means $\text{NH}_3$ gained a proton, so it was the base.
options.C: Incorrect. Neither 2 nor 3 shows $\text{NH}_3$ as an acid. Reaction 2 shows it as a base, and reaction 3 is complex formation where $\text{NH}_3$ is a Lewis base donating a lone pair, with no Brønsted-Lowry proton transfer.
options.D: Correct. Only reaction 1 qualifies, because one $\text{NH}_3$ molecule donates a proton to another to form $\text{NH}_2^-$. This is auto-ionisation, similar to water, where $\text{NH}_3$ is amphoteric and acts as both acid and base.
